operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of products saved in the authenticated customer's wishlist.

The wishlist displays products (not specific variants) that the customer has added for future purchase consideration. Results are ordered by addition date with the newest items appearing first. Products that have been deleted by their sellers are automatically excluded from the listing — they are silently removed from the wishlist without affecting the remaining items.

Each wishlist item in the response includes the referenced product's live information (name, base price or price range, main image) which updates dynamically as the seller edits the product. The wishlist is maintained as a distinct collection separate from the shopping cart — items in the wishlist do not appear in the cart, affect cart totals, or influence checkout processes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the e_commerce_mall_wishlist_items table filtered to the authenticated customer's ID. Apply pagination (page, limit) from the request body. Order by created_at descending (newest first).

Exclude items where deleted_at is not null (soft-deleted items). Additionally, join with e_commerce_mall_products and exclude wishlist items whose referenced product has visibility = 'deleted' — these are products deleted by their sellers and should be automatically filtered from the customer's view.

For each returned wishlist item, include the referenced product's current data: name, base_price, visibility, and the first product image (by sort order) as thumbnail. If the product is deleted_at is not null or visibility is 'deleted', that wishlist item should additionally be soft-deleted (set deleted_at = now()) to reflect the automatic cleanup.

Return a paginated response (IPageIECommerceMallWishlistItem.ISummary) with total count, and the list of summary items. Each summary should contain: wishlist item ID, product ID, product name, product base price, product main image URL, product visibility, and created_at timestamp.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of wishlist items owned by the authenticated customer, sorted by addition date (newest first). Each item includes the live product data (name, base price, main image) and excludes products that have been deleted by their sellers.

requestBody.description: Pagination and sorting parameters for listing the customer's wishlist items. Supports page number, items per page, and optional sort direction. All wishlist items are implicitly scoped to the authenticated customer.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single wishlist item by its unique identifier.

A wishlist item represents a product that a customer has saved for future purchase consideration. This operation returns the complete wishlist item record including the reference to the saved product. The returned data includes the product association at the product level (not variant-specific) and creation metadata.

Only wishlist items belonging to the authenticated customer are accessible. Soft-deleted items — those manually removed by the customer or automatically removed due to the underlying product being deleted by the seller — are excluded from results. If the specified wishlist item does not exist, does not belong to the requesting customer, or has been soft-deleted, a 404 Not Found response is returned without distinguishing the reason.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_wishlist_items table by id matching the wishlistItemId path parameter.

- Filter by the authenticated customer's ID (e_commerce_mall_customer_id) to enforce data isolation — customers can only access their own wishlist items.
- Exclude soft-deleted records: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL.
- Join with e_commerce_mall_products to include product-level information (name, thumbnail image, price range) if the DTO includes nested product data.
- Return 404 Not Found if no matching record is found after applying the customer filter and soft-delete exclusion — do not distinguish between 'not found', 'belongs to another customer', or 'soft-deleted' to prevent information leakage.
- The response should include the full wishlist item entity with all its fields.

responseBody.description: The complete wishlist item entity including the product reference, customer association, and creation and update timestamps.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the wishlist item to retrieve, in UUID format.
parameters.name: wishlistItemId

prerequisites.description: The wishlist item must be created before it can be retrieved. POST /eCommerceMall/customer/wishlist-items adds a product to the customer's wishlist, generating a wishlist item record whose UUID becomes the wishlistItemId path parameter for this GET operation.

operations.description:
Add a product to the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This operation allows a customer to save a product for future purchase consideration. The product is stored at the product level (not variant level), so the customer expresses interest in the product as a whole. Each customer can save a given product only once — attempting to add the same product again results in a conflict error.

The customer is identified from the authenticated session; the request body only needs to specify which product to save. The created wishlist item is returned with its auto-generated ID and creation timestamp.

Wishlist items are ordered newest-first in the customer's wishlist view. If the underlying product is later deleted by the seller, the wishlist item is automatically soft-deleted.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new wishlist item for the authenticated customer.

1. Extract customer ID from the authenticated session context.
2. Validate that the referenced product exists and is not soft-deleted (visibility != 'deleted').
3. Check unique constraint: verify no existing wishlist item exists with the same (customer_id, product_id) and deleted_at IS NULL. If duplicate exists, reject with conflict error.
4. Create the wishlist item record with:
   - id: auto-generated UUID
   - e_commerce_mall_customer_id: authenticated customer's ID
   - e_commerce_mall_product_id: from request body
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
   - deleted_at: null
5. Return the created wishlist item as IECommerceMallWishlistItem.

Edge cases:
- Product not found or deleted: return 404 Not Found
- Duplicate wishlist item (already saved): return 409 Conflict
- Product is in 'deleted' or 'suspended' visibility state: return 422 Unprocessable Entity explaining the product is not available

responseBody.description: The newly created wishlist item with its auto-generated ID, customer reference, product reference, and creation timestamp.

requestBody.description: Product identifier specifying which product to add to the customer's wishlist. The customer is inferred from the authenticated session.

prerequisites.description: The product must exist in the system before a customer can save it to their wishlist. The wishlist item references the product via a foreign key (e_commerce_mall_product_id), and the operation validates that the referenced product exists and is not deleted or suspended.

operations.description:
Remove a product from the customer's wishlist.

This operation allows a customer to manually remove a specific product from their personal wishlist. The removal is performed as a soft delete, preserving the database record for data integrity while excluding it from normal wishlist queries.

If the specified wishlist item does not exist or has already been removed, the operation still completes successfully (idempotent behavior). This ensures that duplicate removal requests or attempts to remove already-removed items do not cause errors.

The operation only removes the wishlist association — the referenced product, its variants, and inventory records remain completely unaffected.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Perform soft delete by setting deleted_at to the current timestamp. Use idempotent logic: if the wishlistItemId does not exist or the record is already soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL), return success without error — do not throw 404 or 4xx. Validate that the authenticated customer owns this wishlist item (e_commerce_mall_customer_id must match the current customer's ID) before performing deletion; if not owned, return 403 Forbidden. Only the owning customer can remove their own wishlist items. After setting deleted_at, update updated_at as well.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the wishlist item to remove (UUID).
parameters.name: wishlistItemId

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated customer's shopping cart contents.

Returns a paginated list of cart items belonging to the currently authenticated customer, ordered by most recently added first. Each cart item includes product name and image, variant option labels (e.g., color, size), current unit price, requested quantity, subtotal, and availability status. Items whose variants have been deleted by the seller or are out of stock are marked as unavailable and excluded from checkout eligibility. When the requested quantity exceeds the available stock, a stock insufficiency warning is included.

Cart items are scoped to the authenticated customer via their session. Soft-deleted (removed) items are excluded from the result set. The response supports cursor or offset-based pagination for large carts.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_cart_items filtered by the authenticated customer's ID (extracted from session/JWT). Exclude soft-deleted items (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL). Join with e_commerce_mall_product_variants for variant pricing and deletion status, e_commerce_mall_products for product name and main image, and e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options for variant option key-value pairs.

For availability determination: mark as unavailable if e_commerce_mall_product_variants.deleted_at IS NOT NULL (variant soft-deleted) OR calculated stock (SUM of e_commerce_mall_inventory_records.quantity changes) <= 0. Include a stock warning flag and the available stock count when cart item quantity > available stock.

Calculate subtotal = quantity × variant price (if variant has an override price, use that; otherwise use the product's base price).

Support pagination with page/limit parameters in the request body. Default sort by created_at descending (newest items first).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cart item summaries containing product name and image URL, variant option labels, current unit price, requested quantity, subtotal, availability status (available/unavailable), stock warning indicator when quantity exceeds available stock, and available stock count.

requestBody.description: Pagination parameters (page number and page size) for controlling the result set. Optional filter criteria and sort configuration for customizing cart item listing order.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single cart item by its unique identifier with full details for cart display.

Returns the cart item record including quantity and timestamps, along with nested product variant information (SKU code, option values, price override, computed stock quantity, and availability status) and nested product information (name, description, base price, main thumbnail image, and visibility state).

The unit price displayed in the cart follows variant pricing logic: if the variant has a non-null price override, that price is used; otherwise the parent product's base_price is inherited. The subtotal is calculated as unit price multiplied by quantity. If the variant is soft-deleted or out of stock (stock quantity is zero), the cart item is marked as unavailable.

The requesting customer's identity must match the cart item's owner — a 403 Forbidden is returned on mismatch. A 404 Not Found is returned if the cart item does not exist, has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is set), or if the identifier is not found.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_cart_items by id with filter deleted_at IS NULL. Verify the requesting customer's id matches e_commerce_mall_customer_id — return 403 Forbidden on mismatch. Join the following relations to build the full response DTO:
- productVariant: includes sku_code, price (nullable for override), deleted_at
- productVariant.product: includes name, description, base_price, visibility
- productVariant.options via e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options (key-value pairs)
- productVariant.inventoryRecords: sum quantity_change to compute current stock
- product.images: get first image by sort_order for thumbnail URL

Compute derived fields: unit_price (variant.price ?? product.base_price), subtotal (unit_price * quantity), is_available (variant.deleted_at IS NULL AND stock > 0). Edge cases: if id not found or deleted_at is not null → 404. If variant.deleted_at is not null or stock is 0 → mark item as unavailable. If variant.price is null → inherit product.base_price.

responseBody.description: Full cart item record with nested product variant and product details. Includes quantity, timestamps, the referenced product variant (SKU code, price override, computed stock, option values, availability), and the parent product (name, description, base price, thumbnail image, visibility). Derived fields include unit price, subtotal, and availability status.

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the cart item to retrieve. Must correspond to an existing, non-deleted cart item record.
parameters.name: cartItemId

operations.description:
Add a product variant to the shopping cart or increase its quantity if already present.

This endpoint adds a specific product variant (SKU) to the authenticated customer's shopping cart. Each cart item represents intent to purchase a defined quantity of one variant. If the customer already has a cart item for the same variant, the requested quantity is combined with the existing quantity rather than creating a duplicate entry.

The product variant must exist and be currently available (not deleted, not out of stock) to be added to the cart. The minimum quantity is 1. The system does not validate stock availability against the final quantity at add time — stock checks occur during checkout.

After addition, the response returns the complete cart item including its current quantity and all timestamps.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Look up the authenticated customer from the session context.
2. Validate that the requested product variant exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null).
3. Validate that the quantity is a positive integer (minimum 1).
4. Query for an existing cart item with the same customer ID and product variant ID combination (leveraging the @@unique composite constraint).
5. If an existing cart item is found: update its quantity by adding the requested quantity to the current quantity, and update the updated_at timestamp.
6. If no existing cart item is found: create a new cart item record with the provided variant ID and quantity, setting created_at and updated_at.
7. Return the final cart item record.

responseBody.description: The full cart item record after the add operation, including the variant reference, current quantity, and system timestamps (created_at, updated_at). If the variant already existed in the cart, this returns the updated item with combined quantity.

requestBody.description: Specifies the product variant to add to the cart and the desired quantity. The variant is identified by its UUID. If the same variant already exists in the customer's cart, the quantity is added to the existing item's quantity rather than creating a duplicate entry.

prerequisites.description: The product variant must exist in the database before it can be added to a customer's shopping cart. This operation creates the variant (SKU) that the cart item references via the required `product_variant_id` field. Without this prerequisite, the cart item creation fails because the foreign key validation requires the variant to exist and not be soft-deleted.

operations.description:
Updates the quantity of a specific cart item identified by its ID.

This operation allows the authenticated customer to change the desired quantity of a product variant in their shopping cart. The cart item must belong to the requesting customer; updates to other customers' cart items are rejected.

If the quantity is set to zero, the cart item is removed from the active cart (soft-deleted) rather than physically deleted, preserving the record for audit purposes.

The update does not validate against current stock availability — customers can increase quantity beyond available stock. The system will mark the item as unavailable during checkout if insufficient stock exists. The product variant must exist in the system; updates to cart items referencing deleted variants are rejected.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the cart item exists and is not already soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL).
2. Validate customer ownership: the cart item's e_commerce_mall_customer_id must match the authenticated customer's ID. Return 403 if mismatched.
3. Validate the requested quantity: must be a non-negative integer.
4. If quantity === 0, soft-delete the cart item (set deleted_at to now) and return the soft-deleted record.
5. If quantity > 0, check stock availability: query the product variant's current stock (sum of inventory records). If the requested quantity exceeds available stock, allow the update but the cart item becomes unavailable (requirements state 'If a variant's stock is less than the cart quantity, a warning is shown' — this is a UI concern, the backend still allows the update).
6. Update the cart item: set quantity = requested value, updated_at = now.
7. If the same variant was already in cart (unique constraint on [customer_id, variant_id]), ensure we're updating the existing record — this is guaranteed by using the cart item ID.
8. Return the updated IECommerceMallCartItem record.

responseBody.description: The updated cart item with the new quantity value and refreshed updated_at timestamp.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the cart item to update. (global scope)
parameters.name: cartItemId

requestBody.description: The new quantity for the cart item. Must be a non-negative integer. Setting quantity to zero removes the item from the cart.

prerequisites.description: The cart item must exist before its quantity can be updated. POST /eCommerceMall/customer/cart-items creates the cart item record and generates the cartItemId UUID that the PUT operation requires as a path parameter. Without a prior POST call, there is no cart item record to reference via {cartItemId}.

operations.description:
Remove a cart item from the customer's shopping cart.

This operation removes a specific cart item identified by its unique ID from the customer's cart. The cart item represents the customer's intent to purchase a particular product variant with a specified quantity. Once removed, the item is no longer included in checkout calculations.

The operation uses soft-deletion, preserving the cart item record with a deletion timestamp for audit and historical purposes. Removal is permitted regardless of the product variant's current availability or stock status — even unavailable or out-of-stock variants can be removed from the cart. After successful removal, the customer's cart total price should be recalculated on the client side by re-fetching the cart data or via the subsequent cart retrieval operation.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Soft-delete the cart item identified by `cartItemId` from the `e_commerce_mall_cart_items` table.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Query the `e_commerce_mall_cart_items` table by `id` to verify the cart item exists and belongs to the authenticated customer.
2. Verify the cart item's `deleted_at` is null — if it is already soft-deleted, return a 404 Not Found (idempotent behavior, the item is effectively gone).
3. Perform a soft delete by setting the `deleted_at` column to the current timestamp. Do NOT physically delete the row from the database.
4. Return the soft-deleted cart item entity as the response body, including all its fields (id, customer_id, variant_id, quantity, created_at, updated_at, and the newly set deleted_at timestamp).

**Business Rules:**
- The cart item can be removed regardless of the variant's availability status or stock condition.
- The customer can only remove their own cart items — verify ownership by checking `e_commerce_mall_customer_id` against the authenticated customer.
- If the cart item does not exist, does not belong to the customer, or is already deleted, return a 404 Not Found error.
- Cart total recalculation is the client's responsibility after successful removal.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the cart item to remove from the cart.
parameters.name: cartItemId

prerequisites.description: The cart item must exist in the system before it can be removed. POST /eCommerceMall/customer/cart-items creates the cart item record (with variant reference and quantity) that this DELETE operation targets via cartItemId.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of the authenticated customer's orders, sorted by newest first.

Each order summary includes the order number, creation date, total price, and the overall order status derived from the statuses of all constituent order items. The overall status is computed as: 'paid' (all items paid), 'shipped' (at least one shipped, none delivered), 'delivered' (all delivered), 'cancelled' (all cancelled), 'refunded' (all refunded), or 'partially_completed' (mixed terminal states).

Filtering is supported by order status to narrow down the results. Pagination controls (page number, page size) are included in the request body. This endpoint is accessible only to authenticated customers.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query e_commerce_mall_orders table filtered by the authenticated customer's ID (e_commerce_mall_customer_id). Apply optional status filter by computing the derived order status from order items at query time - join with e_commerce_mall_order_items and aggregate statuses per order. Apply sorting by created_at descending (newest first). Implement cursor-based or offset pagination as configured. Return paginated summary records with order code, created_at, total_price, and the computed overall status. Edge case: if status filter is provided, pre-filter orders by checking order item statuses before pagination.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order summary records, each containing the order number (code), creation date, total price, and the derived overall order status.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering the order history, including optional order status filter, date range (start and end), and pagination parameters (page, limit).

operations.description:
Retrieve full order details by order number.

This endpoint returns the complete order record including all purchased items, snapshots preserved at the time of purchase, shipping address, and shipment tracking information. Each order item includes the product name, variant options (e.g., "Color: Red, Size: Large"), quantity, unit price, and its independent fulfillment status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded). The product-variant snapshot and seller profile snapshot captured at purchase time are also included for historical accuracy. Shipment entries provide carrier name, tracking number, shipped timestamp, and delivery confirmation status.

Customers can view their own orders only. If the requested order does not belong to the requesting customer, the request is rejected. Administrators can view any order on the platform for oversight and dispute resolution purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the `e_commerce_mall_orders` table by the unique `code` field (string equality lookup). Join with the following relations to build the full response:
- `orderItems`: List of purchased order items with quantity, unit_price, status
- `orderItems.productVariantSnapshot` (e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots): Immutable product name, description, base price, variant SKU, variant options, variant price
- `orderItems.sellerSnapshot` (e_commerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots): Immutable shop name and logo
- `orderItems.shipmentItem.shipment` (e_commerce_mall_shipment_items → e_commerce_mall_shipments): Carrier name, tracking number, shipped_at, delivered_at

Authorization logic (handled at controller layer):
- Customer actor: Verify `order.e_commerce_mall_customer_id` matches the authenticated customer's ID. Reject with 404 (not 403) if mismatch to avoid leaking order existence.
- Administrator actor: Allow access regardless of customer_id.

Return 404 if no order matches the given orderCode.

Do NOT include deleted/soft-deleted records where `deleted_at` is non-null for shipments. Order items and orders themselves are preserved permanently even after customer account deletion.

responseBody.description: Complete order record including all purchased items with their product-variant snapshots, seller profile snapshots, shipping address snapshot, and shipment tracking information.

parameters.description: Unique order number assigned at order creation for customer reference and communication purposes. (global scope)
parameters.name: orderCode

operations.description:
Place an order by checking out the current cart items.

The customer selects a shipping address from their saved addresses and confirms the purchase. The system validates all cart items for availability and stock sufficiency, processes payment through an external payment gateway, and upon successful payment creates the order with all checked-out items as individual order items. Each order item receives status 'paid' and purchase-time snapshots are automatically captured to preserve the product details, variant configuration, and seller profile information as they existed at the moment of purchase for historical accuracy.

Stock quantities are decreased for each purchased variant, and purchased items are removed from the cart. If payment processing fails, no order is created and the customer can retry without losing their order summary selections. The overall order status is derived from the individual order item statuses after creation.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Authenticate the customer from the session. Fetch the customer's current cart items with their product variants. Validate each cart item: variant must not be deleted (deleted_at is null) and must have sufficient stock (sum of inventory_records quantity_change >= cart item quantity). Fetch the selected shipping address by addressId from request body — verify it belongs to this customer and is not soft-deleted. Calculate total price by summing (cartItem.quantity * variant.price or product.base_price) across all valid cart items. Process payment via external payment gateway integration — if payment fails, return an error (HTTP 402 or similar) without creating any records. If payment succeeds: create the order with a unique auto-generated order code, total price, and address snapshot fields copied from the customer's address. For each distinct variant in the cart (combining quantities since multiple cart items for same variant are already combined by the unique constraint), create an order item with quantity, unit_price (from variant), and status 'paid'. Create three snapshots per order item: (1) product snapshot capturing current product name, description, base_price, category assignment, and all variant snapshots; (2) order item snapshot capturing product_name, product_description, product_base_price, variant_sku, variant_options (formatted string), variant_price; (3) seller profile snapshot capturing shop_name and shop_logo. Create negative inventory records for each variant with quantity_change = -(orderItem.quantity) and reason = 'order placed - Order #{code}'. Remove all checked-out cart items (set deleted_at). Return the created order with all items, snapshots, and calculated overall order status. Edge cases: empty cart → reject (HTTP 422); no shipping address provided → reject; cart contains unavailable items → reject with details of which items are unavailable; payment gateway timeout → return server error.

responseBody.description: The newly created order with full details including the order number, total price, shipping address snapshot, all order items with their individual statuses, purchase-time snapshots for each item (product, variant, seller profile), and the derived overall order status.

requestBody.description: Selection of the shipping address to use for this order. The customer picks one of their saved addresses by its ID. All cart items belonging to this customer are implicitly included as the items to purchase.

prerequisites.description: A shipping address must exist before an order can reference it. The customer creates one or more addresses via this endpoint, then selects one by addressId during checkout. Without a saved address, the order creation fails because no valid addressId can be provided.

Cart items must exist in the customer's cart to be checked out into order items. The customer adds product variants to their cart via this endpoint. Without cart items, the order creation is rejected with 'empty cart' (HTTP 422).

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of order items within a specific order.

This endpoint returns the line items belonging to an order identified by its unique order code. Each order item represents a purchased product variant with its quantity, unit price, current fulfillment status, and links to the purchased product variant.

Access control: Customers can only view items from their own orders. Sellers can only view items belonging to their products within the order. Administrators can view all items in any order. The system automatically filters results based on the authenticated user's identity and permissions.

Results can be filtered by item status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) and are returned with cursor-based or offset-based pagination. Items are sorted by creation date in descending order (newest first) by default.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Resolve the order by its unique `code` field. If no order with the given code exists, return 404 Not Found.

Apply actor-based data filtering automatically:
- Customer: join with e_commerce_mall_orders and filter by e_commerce_mall_customer_id matching the authenticated customer
- Seller: join through e_commerce_mall_product_variants → e_commerce_mall_products and filter by seller_id matching the authenticated seller
- Administrator: no additional filter (view all)

Apply search/filter criteria from the request body:
- `status` filter: match against e_commerce_mall_order_items.status field (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded)
- Pagination: support page/limit or cursor-based pagination
- Sorting: default sort by created_at descending; support sort by status, created_at

Join with e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots to include the product name, variant SKU, and variant options in each summary record. Join with e_commerce_mall_product_variants for current stock status.

Return 200 with paginated results containing order item summaries. Return empty page if no items match the criteria.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item summary records within the specified order, filtered according to the authenticated user's access permissions and the provided search criteria.

parameters.description: Unique order code identifying the order whose items to retrieve. This is the human-readable order number assigned at order creation, not the internal UUID.
parameters.name: orderCode

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering order items within the specified order. Supports filtering by item status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) and standard pagination parameters (page, limit).

operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of a specific order item within a customer order.

This endpoint returns comprehensive information about a single order item, including the historical snapshots captured at the time of purchase — the product name, description, base price, variant SKU and option values, and the seller's shop name and logo. When the item has been shipped, tracking information (carrier name, tracking number, shipped and delivered timestamps) is also included. The item's full status history is provided for audit purposes.

The order is identified by its human-readable order code (not the internal UUID), making it convenient for customer support and reference. The item is identified by its unique UUID.

This data is available to the customer who placed the order, the seller who sold the product, and platform administrators for order oversight and dispute resolution.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_order_items by UUID (itemId) after verifying the item belongs to the order identified by orderCode (join through e_commerce_mall_orders using the unique code constraint).

Join the following related data:
- e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots (product-variant snapshot): product_name, product_description, product_base_price, variant_sku, variant_options, variant_price
- e_commerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots (seller snapshot): shop_name, shop_logo
- e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs (status history): from_status, to_status, reason, created_at — ordered chronologically
- e_commerce_mall_shipment_items → e_commerce_mall_shipments (tracking info): carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, delivered_at (nullable)

Handle 404 errors: if orderCode does not match any order, or if itemId does not match any order item within that order, return a 404 Not Found. Handle 403: if the requesting actor is a customer, verify the order belongs to that customer (e_commerce_mall_orders.e_commerce_mall_customer_id). If the requesting actor is a seller, verify the item's variant belongs to that seller (through e_commerce_mall_product_variants → e_commerce_mall_products → seller_id). Administrators can access any order item.

responseBody.description: Full order item details including product-variant snapshot, seller snapshot, shipment tracking information, and status history. Contains historical data captured at the time of purchase such as product name, description, base price, variant SKU, variant options, variant price override, seller shop name, and shop logo URL.

parameters.description: The unique order code identifying the parent order. (global scope)
parameters.name: orderCode

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the order item to retrieve.
parameters.name: itemId

operations.description:
Search and list order items with filtering, pagination, and sorting.

Retrieves order items based on configurable search criteria. The scope of returned items depends on the authenticated user's role: customers see only order items belonging to their own orders, sellers see only order items for products they own, and administrators see all order items across the platform.

Each returned order item includes summary information about the purchased product variant, quantity, unit price, current status, and the parent order reference. Results are paginated and can be filtered by order item status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded), creation date range, and associated order code.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_order_items table with role-based data scoping:
- Customer: JOIN with e_commerce_mall_orders WHERE customer_id = authenticated customer ID
- Seller: JOIN with e_commerce_mall_product_variants → e_commerce_mall_products WHERE seller_id = authenticated seller ID
- Administrator: No scope restriction — all order items visible

Apply search filters from request body:
- status filter: filter by current order item status (paid/shipped/delivered/cancelled/refunded), supports multiple values (OR logic)
- created_at range: filter by order item creation timestamp range (gte/lte)
- orderCode: substring match against parent order's code field
- variantSku: substring match against variant SKU via e_commerce_mall_product_variants relationship

Support cursor-based or offset pagination from request body. Sort by created_at descending by default, with configurable sort field and direction.

Include computed fields in summary: product name (from the order item snapshot or variants relationship), seller shop name (from seller snapshot), variant options text.

Return empty page array if no results match the criteria. Do not expose order items belonging to other customers or sellers based on role restrictions.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item summary records, each containing the product name, variant options, quantity, unit price, subtotal, current status, and parent order reference. Results are scoped to the authenticated user's data access permissions.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering order items. Supports filtering by status, creation date range, associated order code, and variant SKU. Includes pagination and sorting parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single order item by its unique identifier.

Returns the complete order item record including all related data captured at the time of purchase. The response includes the parent order's shipping address and customer association, the purchased product variant details (SKU, options, pricing), as well as immutable snapshots preserving the product name, description, variant options, and seller shop identity exactly as they existed when the order was placed. Each order item has its own independent status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded) tracked through a status log history.

Customers can use this endpoint to view detailed information about a specific item within their order history. Sellers can inspect individual line items sold from their shop. Administrators can access any order item for oversight and dispute resolution purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query e_commerce_mall_order_items by id (UUID). Join with e_commerce_mall_orders to include shipping address fields (recipient name, phone, street, city, state, postal code, country) and customer association. Join with e_commerce_mall_product_variants to include the variant's SKU code, option configuration, and pricing. Join with e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots (1:1 via e_commerce_mall_order_item_id) to include product_name, product_description, product_base_price, variant_sku, variant_options, variant_price at the time of purchase. Join with e_commerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots (1:1 via e_commerce_mall_order_item_id) to include the seller's shop_name and shop_logo at the time of purchase. operations.description:
Retrieve the complete status change history for a specific order item.

This endpoint returns a paginated, chronological list of all status transitions that have occurred for a given order item, providing a full audit trail of its lifecycle. Each log entry records the transition from one status to another — including the from_status (previous state), to_status (new state), reason for the change, and precise timestamp.

The status log is essential for tracking an order item's fulfillment progress from initial payment through shipping, delivery, and any cancellations or refunds. The audit trail supports customer inquiries, seller operations, and administrator oversight by providing transparency into when and why each status change occurred. The 'shipped' status entry's timestamp is the reference point for the 14-day auto-delivery window.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query the e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs table filtered by e_commerce_mall_order_item_id matching the {itemId} path parameter. Support pagination (page, limit) with default ordering by created_at descending (newest first). Support optional filtering by: to_status (enum: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded), from_status, reason, and date range (created_at_from, created_at_to). Verify the parent order item exists in e_commerce_mall_order_items — return 404 if not found. Authorization rules: customers can view status logs of their own order items (verify via the order → customer relationship chain); sellers can view status logs of order items containing their products (verify via product_variant → product → seller relationship); administrators can view all status logs. Return 404 if the parent order item (itemId) does not exist.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item status log entries, each representing a single status transition with from_status, to_status, reason, and timestamp, ordered from newest to oldest.

parameters.name: itemId

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific status change history entry for an order item.

Order item status logs record every status transition in an order item's lifecycle — from initial payment through shipping, delivery, cancellation, or refund. Each log entry captures the previous status, the new status, the reason for the change, and the exact timestamp when the transition occurred.

This endpoint returns a single status log entry identified by its unique ID, scoped to a specific parent order item. The `itemId` path parameter ensures the log belongs to the correct order item, providing data isolation so that one order item's status logs cannot be accessed through another item's identifier.

Typical reasons captured in status logs include: "shipment_created" (when shipped via a seller shipment), "customer_delivery_confirmation" (customer confirmed delivery), "auto_delivery_timeout" (14-day auto-delivery), "cancellation_approved" (seller approved cancellation), "refund_approved" (seller approved refund), and "administrator_force_cancel" or "administrator_force_refund" (admin actions).
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs table filtering by both id = logId AND e_commerce_mall_order_item_id = itemId. The itemId scope ensures data isolation — verify the log belongs to the specified order item. Return 404 Not Found if no status log matches both criteria. Status logs are immutable once created, so no transactional concerns or race conditions apply. No joins are required unless the caller additionally needs the parent order item's current status, which can be added as optional query parameter expansion. The from_status field may be null for the initial 'paid' status entry. The to_status field is always non-null representing the new state after transition.

responseBody.description: The status log entry containing the previous and new status values, the reason for the transition, and timestamps for when the change occurred.

operations.description:
Create a new shipment containing one or more order items from the seller's own products.

When a seller creates a shipment, they select the paid order items they wish to include, enter the carrier name and tracking number for the package. Upon successful creation, all included order items automatically transition from 'paid' to 'shipped' status. Multiple order items from the same seller can be bundled into a single shipment, or each item can be shipped individually in separate shipments.

Only sellers with 'approved' approval status can create shipments. Only order items belonging to the creating seller with 'paid' status can be selected. Each order item can be assigned to at most one shipment at a time.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a shipment for the authenticated seller.

1. Verify the authenticated seller's `approval_status` is 'approved' — reject with appropriate error if pending or rejected.
2. For each `orderItemId` in the request:
   a. Load the `e_commerce_mall_order_items` record.
   b. Verify the order item's `e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id` belongs to a product owned by this seller (check via `e_commerce_mall_products.seller_id`).
   c. Verify the order item's `status` is 'paid' — reject if any other status.
   d. Verify there is no existing `e_commerce_mall_shipment_items` record for this order item — reject if already in another shipment.
3. Validate at least one order item was provided — reject empty list.
4. Create the `e_commerce_mall_shipments` record with the seller_id, carrier_name, tracking_number, and shipped_at set to current timestamp.
5. Create `e_commerce_mall_shipment_items` records linking each selected order item to the new shipment.
6. Update all included order items' status to 'shipped' and record status changes in `e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs`.
7. Return the created shipment with its associated items.

Edge cases: If any validation fails (wrong seller, wrong status, already shipped, empty list), reject the entire operation — no partial shipment creation.

responseBody.description: The newly created shipment with full details including carrier info, shipment timestamp, and the associated shipment items linking to the bundled order items.

requestBody.description: Shipment creation details including the list of order item IDs to include, carrier name, and tracking number for the package.

operations.description:
Search and list shipments with filtering and pagination.

This endpoint allows sellers to view their dispatched shipments, customers to view shipments associated with their orders for tracking purposes, and administrators to view all shipments across the platform for oversight. Each shipment represents a physical package containing one or more order items from the same seller, with shared carrier name, tracking number, and shipment/delivery timestamps.

Results are paginated and sorted by shipment creation date (newest first by default). Optional filters narrow results by carrier name, tracking number, shipment date range, delivery status (shipped or delivered), and delivery date range. Access is automatically scoped by actor type through authentication — sellers see only their own shipments, customers see shipments tied to their orders, and administrators see all shipments.

Soft-deleted shipments are excluded from results unless explicitly requested by administrators.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the e_commerce_mall_shipments table with pagination and optional search filters.

Apply actor-based authorization scoping:
- Seller: filter by seller_id matching the authenticated seller's ID
- Customer: join through e_commerce_mall_shipment_items → e_commerce_mall_order_items → e_commerce_mall_orders, filter by e_commerce_mall_orders.e_commerce_mall_customer_id matching the authenticated customer
- Administrator: no seller/customer filter — view all shipments across the platform

Search filters (all optional, applied via AND logic):
- carrierName: partial/fuzzy match on carrier_name field
- trackingNumber: partial/fuzzy match on tracking_number field
- shippedAtFrom/shippedAtTo: date range filter on shipped_at timestamp
- deliveredAtFrom/deliveredAtTo: date range filter on delivered_at timestamp
- deliveryStatus: enum filter — 'shipped' (delivered_at IS NULL) or 'delivered' (delivered_at IS NOT NULL)

Soft-delete handling: exclude records where deleted_at IS NOT NULL by default. Administrators may optionally include soft-deleted records.

Include standard pagination parameters: page (1-based index), limit (items per page), and sort (field and direction). Default sort is by created_at descending.

Return summary fields for each shipment: id, carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, delivered_at, and the count of associated order items (aggregated from e_commerce_mall_shipment_items).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment summary records, each containing the shipment ID, carrier name, tracking number, shipment timestamp, delivery timestamp, and count of associated order items for list display.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering shipments, including carrier name, tracking number, shipment and delivery date ranges, delivery status filter, and standard pagination parameters (page, limit, sort).

operations.description:
Retrieve a single shipment by its unique identifier.

Returns the complete shipment record including carrier name, tracking number, shipping timestamp, and delivery confirmation timestamp. The response also includes all order items contained within this shipment, each with its product variant reference, quantity, unit price at the time of purchase, and current fulfillment status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded).

operations.description:
Confirm delivery of a shipment package, marking all contained order items as delivered.

When a customer receives a physical package from the shipping carrier, they confirm delivery through this endpoint. Upon successful confirmation, the system records the delivery timestamp on the shipment record and simultaneously transitions every order item grouped in that shipment to the 'delivered' status. This bulk status change affects all order items in the shipment together — individual item confirmation is not supported.

Only shipments that have been dispatched by the seller (shipped_at is set) and are not yet delivered (delivered_at is null) can be confirmed. If delivery was already confirmed or the shipment has not been shipped, the operation is rejected with an appropriate error.

Each status transition is recorded in the order item status change log with reason 'customer_delivery_confirmation', providing a complete audit trail. If the customer does not manually confirm delivery within 14 days of the shipment's shipped_at timestamp, an automatic batch process transitions the shipment to delivered state instead.

Accessible to: authenticated customers who own the order that contains this shipment.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate the shipment exists by shipmentId. Verify the shipment belongs to the authenticated customer by joining: e_commerce_mall_shipment_items → e_commerce_mall_order_items → e_commerce_mall_orders → e_commerce_mall_customer_id. Compare customer_id against the authenticated customer's identity.

Pre-condition checks (return appropriate HTTP errors):
- Shipment not found → 404 Not Found
- Shipment belongs to a different customer's orders → 403 Forbidden
- Shipment not yet dispatched (shipped_at is null) → 422 Unprocessable Entity
- Shipment already delivered (delivered_at is not null) → 409 Conflict

Transactional execution:
1. Begin database transaction with row-level lock on the shipment record (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) to prevent double-confirmation race conditions
2. Update e_commerce_mall_shipments: SET delivered_at = NOW(), updated_at = NOW()
3. Query all e_commerce_mall_shipment_items WHERE shipment_id = {shipmentId}
4. For each linked e_commerce_mall_order_item:
   a. Update status to 'delivered'
   b. Insert status log: from_status='shipped', to_status='delivered', reason='customer_delivery_confirmation'
5. Commit transaction
6. Return the updated shipment record with all relations for confirmation display

Edge cases:
- Order items already in 'cancelled' or 'refunded' status within the shipment → skip those items (they reached terminal states before shipment)
- Order items already 'delivered' → skip (idempotent within the batch)
- Empty shipment_items (no items linked) → reject with 422 Unprocessable Entity
- Auto-delivery timeout (14 days) is handled by a separate scheduled job, not this endpoint

responseBody.description: The updated shipment record reflecting the delivery confirmation, including the set delivered_at timestamp. All contained order items have been transitioned to 'delivered' status with corresponding status log entries for audit purposes.

operations.description:
Search and list order items within a specific shipment with filtering and pagination.

This operation allows the seller who created the shipment to view all order items packed in that shipment package. Each shipment item record links a shipment to an order item from the seller's own products. Results include order item details such as product name, variant options, quantity, unit price, and current item status.

Sellers can filter items by order item status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) to track fulfillment progress. Results are paginated with configurable page size and cursor for efficient browsing of shipments containing many items.

Only the seller who owns the shipment can access this endpoint — items from other sellers are never associated with this shipment.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_shipment_items table filtered by shipment_id = {shipmentId}.

Join with:
  - e_commerce_mall_order_items (for quantity, unit_price, status, created_at)
  - e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots (for preserved product name and variant details at time of purchase)
  - e_commerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots (for preserved seller shop name)

Authorization: Only the seller who owns the shipment (seller_id on the shipment record) can access this endpoint. Verify the authenticated seller's ID matches the shipment's seller_id.

Filtering:
  - Order item status filter (paid/shipped/delivered/cancelled/refunded)
  - Date range filter on shipment item created_at

Pagination: Use cursor-based pagination with configurable limit (default 20, max 100).

Sorting: By default, sort by created_at descending (newest first). Allow sorting by order item status or quantity.

Edge cases:
  - Shipment not found: return 404
  - Shipment belongs to different seller: return 403 Forbidden
  - Shipment has no items yet (deleted items): return empty list

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment item summaries. Each item includes the order item's product details, variant information, quantity, unit price, and current status.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific order item within the context of its parent shipment.

This endpoint returns the complete details of an individual order item that has been packed and shipped as part of a shipment. The response includes the order item's purchased product variant information (name, SKU, options), quantity, unit price captured at the time of purchase, current fulfillment status, and the shipment's tracking information including carrier name, tracking number, shipped timestamp, and delivery confirmation timestamp.

**Access Control**:
- Customers can only retrieve items from shipments belonging to their own orders
- Sellers can only retrieve items from shipments they created (containing their own products)
- Administrators can retrieve any shipment item on the platform

**Relationships**: Each order item can be assigned to at most one shipment, enforced by a unique constraint on the junction table. When a shipment is created, all included order items transition to `shipped` status. When delivery is confirmed per shipment, all items in that shipment transition to `delivered` status together. The shipmentId parameter provides contextual verification that the item belongs to the specified shipment.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the e_commerce_mall_shipment_items junction table to find the record where shipment_id = shipmentId AND order_item_id = itemId. If not found, return 404 NotFound.

Join with e_commerce_mall_shipments to get carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, delivered_at, and seller_id.
Join with e_commerce_mall_order_items to get quantity, unit_price, status, e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id, and e_commerce_mall_order_id.
Join with e_commerce_mall_product_variants to get SKU code and variant option values.
Join with e_commerce_mall_products to get product name, seller_id.
Join with e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots for preserved product/variant details at time of purchase.

Authorization (applied after query):
- Customer: verify e_commerce_mall_order_items.e_commerce_mall_order_id belongs to the authenticated customer
- Seller: verify e_commerce_mall_shipments.seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID
- Administrator: allow access to any shipment item
- Return 403 Forbidden if authorization fails

Edge cases:
- The order item may have been soft-deleted (deleted_at set) — still return it for order history purposes
- If shipment is soft-deleted (deleted_at set), still return for historical reference
- Return comprehensive error messages for not-found vs forbidden scenarios

responseBody.description: Complete details of an order item within its shipment context. operations.description:
Search and list cancellation requests with filtering and pagination support.

This endpoint allows authenticated users to search through cancellation requests based on various filter criteria. The results depend on the caller's role: customers see only their own cancellation requests, sellers see requests for order items containing their products, and administrators see all requests across the platform.

Filtering capabilities include status (pending, approved, rejected), creation date range, and association filters. Results are paginated and sorted by creation date in descending order by default.

Each cancellation request summary in the list includes the request status, reason, timestamps, and references to the associated order item and customer.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests table with pagination and filtering.

Apply search filters from request body:
- status filter (single or multiple): pending, approved, rejected
- created_at date range (from/to)
- customer_id filter (administrators and sellers scoping)
- seller_id filter (administrators scoping)
- order_item_id filter (for specific item lookup)

Authorization:
- Customers: scope results to e_commerce_mall_customer_id = authenticated customer ID
- Sellers: scope results via join with e_commerce_mall_order_items → e_commerce_mall_product_variants → e_commerce_mall_products where seller_id = authenticated seller ID
- Administrators: view all cancellation requests
- Super administrators: view all cancellation requests

Join with e_commerce_mall_order_items for order item details and with e_commerce_mall_customers, e_commerce_mall_sellers for actor display names.

Pagination: Use cursor-based or offset-based pagination with page/limit parameters from request body.
Sorting: Default sort by created_at descending. Support sort by created_at, status.

Return paginated list of cancellation request summaries with computed fields for display.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cancellation request summaries containing status, reason, timestamps, and associated order item information for display in list views.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for cancellation requests including status filters, date range, pagination parameters, and sorting options. The available filters may be scoped by the caller's role automatically.

operations.description:

Cancellation requests are customer-initiated requests to cancel a paid order item before it has been shipped. Each request is associated with exactly one order item and includes the customer's reason for cancellation, the current status (pending, approved, or rejected), and seller response details if the seller has responded.

Use this endpoint to view the current state of a specific cancellation request for customer support, order management, or status tracking purposes.

Query the e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests table by primary key (id) using the provided cancellationRequestId path parameter.

- Customers can only access their own cancellation requests (where e_commerce_mall_customer_id matches their customer account)
- Sellers can only access cancellation requests for order items containing their products (where e_commerce_mall_seller_id matches or the order item's variant belongs to them)

operations.description:
Submit a cancellation request for a specific order item.

Customers can request cancellation of individual order items that are in the paid status (payment completed, not yet shipped). Each cancellation request targets exactly one order item. The request includes a free-form reason explaining why the customer wishes to cancel.

Upon submission, the request enters pending status and awaits review by the seller who owns the product variant in the target order item. The customer's identity and session are automatically associated with the request for audit purposes.

A cancellation request can only be created when the order item is in the paid status. Items that are shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded are not eligible for cancellation. An order item must not already have an active pending cancellation request.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests record.

1. Validate the target order item exists via e_commerce_mall_order_item_id.
2. Verify the order item belongs to the authenticated customer (check e_commerce_mall_orders → e_commerce_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer).
3. Verify the order item's status is "paid" — only paid items can be cancelled. Reject with error if status is shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded.
4. Check that no existing cancellation request for the same order item has status "pending" — prevent duplicate pending requests.
5. Set e_commerce_mall_customer_id from the authenticated customer's identity.
6. Set e_commerce_mall_customer_session_id from the authenticated session.
7. Set reason from the request body.
8. Set status to "pending".
9. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp.
10. Return the created IECommerceMallCancellationRequest record.

Edge cases:
- If the order item does not exist, return 404 Not Found.
- If the order item does not belong to the authenticated customer, return 403 Forbidden.
- If the order item is not in paid status, return 422 Unprocessable Entity with a message indicating the item is not eligible for cancellation.
- If a pending cancellation request already exists for this order item, return 409 Conflict.

responseBody.description: The newly created cancellation request with pending status, including the customer's reason and the associated order item reference.

requestBody.description: The order item to cancel and the reason for cancellation. The customer's identity and session are determined from the authentication context.

prerequisites.description: The order item must exist before a cancellation request can reference it. POST /eCommerceMall/customer/orders creates the order with all order items, which the customer can then cancel individually.

operations.description:
Respond to a pending cancellation request by approving or rejecting it.

This endpoint allows the seller who owns the product variant associated with the order item to respond to a customer's cancellation request. The seller reviews the customer's reason and decides whether to accept or decline the cancellation.

When the seller approves the request, the order item is cancelled, and the stock quantity for the corresponding product variant is restored via an automatic inventory record. A snapshot of the cancellation request state is captured at the moment of response for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

When the seller rejects the request, the order item continues processing normally, and the seller may optionally provide a rejection reason explaining their decision. The response is also preserved in a snapshot.

The cancellation request must be in 'pending' status. Only the seller who owns the product variant in the target order item may respond.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Validate that the cancellation request exists and is in 'pending' status. Validate that the authenticated seller owns the product variant associated with the order item. Update the cancellation request: set seller_id (current seller), seller_session_id (current session), status (approved or rejected), responded_at (current timestamp), and optionally rejection_reason (if rejected). Create a cancellation_request_snapshot recording the reason, status, and timestamp. If approved: update the associated order_item's status to 'cancelled', create an inventory_record with positive quantity change equal to the cancelled item's quantity and reason 'cancellation_approval'. Use a database transaction to ensure atomicity across all updates. If rejected: no further side effects beyond recording the response.

prerequisites.description: The cancellation request must be created by the customer before the seller can respond to it. Without this prerequisite, the seller's respond operation would find no cancellation request to act upon.

operations.description:
Search and list refund requests with filtering, sorting, and pagination.

This endpoint provides a comprehensive search interface for refund requests across the platform. It serves three distinct actor types with appropriate data scoping: customers view their own submitted refund requests, sellers view refund requests targeting their products (enabling them to approve or reject), and administrators gain full visibility into all refund requests for platform oversight.

Results are paginated and sorted by newest first by default. The response includes summary information such as the refund reason, current status, response timestamp (if the seller has responded), and related order item and customer/seller identifiers. Use the optional filter parameters to narrow results by status, date range, or specific customers and sellers.

Soft-deleted refund requests are excluded from results by default.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_refund_returns table with pagination, filtering, and sorting.

## Authentication & Data Isolation
- **Customers**: Automatically scope query by `e_commerce_mall_customer_id = current customer id`. Customers can only see their own refund requests.
- **Sellers**: Automatically scope query by `e_commerce_mall_seller_id = current seller id`. Sellers can only see refund requests for their own products.
- **Administrators**: No automatic scoping. Can search across all refund requests. Can filter by `customerId` and `sellerId` parameters.

## Filtering
Apply the following optional filters from the request body:
- `status`: Filter by refund request status (pending, approved, rejected). Single value or array.
- `fromCreatedAt` / `toCreatedAt`: Date range filter on `created_at` column.
- `customerId`: (Admin only) Filter by specific customer.
- `sellerId`: (Admin only) Filter by specific seller.
- `orderItemId`: Filter by specific order item.
- `search`: Text search on the `reason` field (partial match).

## Sorting
Default sort: `created_at` descending (newest first). Support sort by other fields: `created_at`, `status`, `response_timestamp`.

## Pagination
Use cursor-based or offset pagination with `page` and `limit` parameters. Return total count for UI pagination display.

## Joins & Enrichment
Join with `e_commerce_mall_order_items` to display product/variant info. Join with `e_commerce_mall_customers` for customer name/email. Join with `e_commerce_mall_sellers` for seller shop name. Join with `e_commerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots` to indicate if a snapshot exists.

## Edge Cases
- Include soft-deleted refund requests (`deleted_at IS NULL` filter) unless admin explicitly requests to see deleted records.
- If the authenticated actor has neither customer, seller, nor admin role, reject with 403 Forbidden.
- Return empty page array (not error) when no refund requests match criteria.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering refund requests. Supports filtering by status, creation date range, customer, seller, and order item. Includes pagination and sorting parameters.

Retrieve a specific refund request by its unique identifier.

Returns the full details of a refund request including the customer's stated reason for seeking a refund, the current processing status, and the seller's response timestamp if a decision has already been made. The refund request references a single delivered order item for which the customer is requesting a refund within the statutory 7-day refund window.

Each refund request is associated with three key actors: the customer who submitted it, the seller who must respond, and the order item being contested. The status field indicates where the request is in its lifecycle — pending (awaiting seller response), approved (refund granted), or rejected (refund denied). When the seller responds, an immutable snapshot of the request state is automatically created for audit trail purposes.

Query e_commerce_mall_refund_requests table by id matching the refundRequestId path parameter. If no active record is found (matching id and deleted_at IS NULL), return 404 Not Found.

Include the following columns in the response: id, e_commerce_mall_order_item_id, e_commerce_mall_customer_id, e_commerce_mall_seller_id, reason, status, response_timestamp, created_at, updated_at. The deleted_at column is excluded — only active (non-deleted) records are returned.

Authorization at the middleware layer should enforce that:
- Customers can only view their own refund requests (where e_commerce_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer's id)
- Sellers can only view refund requests for their own products (where e_commerce_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller's id)
- Administrators and super administrators can view any refund request

Edge cases: If the refund request references an order item that was soft-deleted (deleted_at not null), the request itself is still accessible as long as the refund request record is active.

Returns the full details of a refund request including the customer's stated reason for seeking a refund, the current processing status, and the seller's response timestamp if a decision has already been made. The refund request references a single delivered order item for which the customer is requesting a refund within the statutory 7-day refund window.

- Sellers can only view refund requests for their own products (where e_commerce_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller's id)
- Administrators and super administrators can view any refund request

operations.description:
Create a new refund request for a specific delivered order item.

A refund request allows a customer to seek a refund for an individual order item that has been delivered. Each refund request targets exactly one order item and requires a textual reason explaining why the refund is being requested. Only order items with status "delivered" are eligible, and the request must be submitted within 7 calendar days of the delivery date. A customer may submit at most one refund request per order item — duplicate pending requests are prevented.

When created, the refund request enters "pending" status and awaits the seller's decision. The seller may either approve (triggering payment reversal and stock restoration) or reject the request. A snapshot of the request state is created at the time of seller response for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

**Security**: The authenticated customer making the request must be the owner of the order item. The seller identity is automatically derived from the order item's product variant ownership chain.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate that the authenticated customer matches the customer who owns the order item identified by `orderItemId`. Query `e_commerce_mall_order_items` by ID and verify `e_commerce_mall_customer_id` matches the authenticated user.

Verify eligibility: the order item's `status` must equal "delivered".

Verify the 7-day refund window: calculate the time elapsed from the delivery timestamp (use `e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs` to find when status changed to "delivered", or use `updated_at` of the order item as proxy) to the current timestamp. Reject if more than 7 calendar days have elapsed.

Enforce the unique constraint: query `e_commerce_mall_refund_requests` where `e_commerce_mall_order_item_id` matches. If a record already exists with status "pending", reject the duplicate request.

Derive `e_commerce_mall_seller_id` from the order item's variant→product→seller chain: `orderItem.productVariant.product.seller.id`.

Create the refund request with: `e_commerce_mall_order_item_id` from input, `e_commerce_mall_customer_id` from authenticated customer, `e_commerce_mall_seller_id` derived from variant, `reason` from input, `status` = "pending", `response_timestamp` = null.

Return the full created refund request record. On validation failure, return appropriate error messages indicating which condition was not met (not delivered, outside 7-day window, duplicate request, not the item owner).

responseBody.description: The newly created refund request record with "pending" status, awaiting seller response.

requestBody.description: The order item identifier and the refund reason required to create a refund request. The customer identity is automatically determined from the authenticated user.

prerequisites.description: The order item being refunded must already exist. Order items are created when an order is placed through this operation. Without a pre-existing order item in 'delivered' status, no refund request can be submitted.

operations.description:
Responds to a pending refund request by either approving or rejecting it.

This operation allows a seller to review and respond to a refund request submitted by a customer for a delivered order item. The seller provides their decision by specifying a new status of either "approved" or "rejected".

When the seller approves the refund request, the system automatically processes the refund: the order item's status transitions to "refunded", the associated product variant's stock is restored by a positive inventory record matching the purchased quantity (with reason "refund"), and a snapshot of the refund request state is preserved for audit purposes.

When the seller rejects the refund request, the request status is set to "rejected", a snapshot is created, and the order item remains in its "delivered" state without any stock or financial changes.

Only the seller who owns the product variant in the refunded order item can respond to the refund request. Only refund requests in "pending" status are eligible for a response.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate the refund request exists and is owned by the seller (e_commerce_mall_refund_requests.seller_id matches authenticated seller).

Validate the current status is 'pending' — only pending requests can be responded to.

Validate the request body contains a valid decision: status must be 'approved' or 'rejected'.

When status is 'approved':
- Update refund_request status to 'approved' and set response_timestamp to current time.
- Create a refund_request_snapshot with the customer's reason, decision, and response timestamp.
- Restore stock: create a positive inventory_record on the associated product_variant with quantity matching the order_item.quantity, reason = 'refund'.
- Update the order_item status to 'refunded'.

When status is 'rejected':
- Update refund_request status to 'rejected' and set response_timestamp to current time.
- Create a refund_request_snapshot with the customer's reason, decision, and response timestamp.
- The order_item remains in 'delivered' status; no stock restoration occurs.

Use a database transaction to ensure atomicity of the status update, snapshot creation, inventory record, and order item status change.

Edge cases:
- If the refund request is not in 'pending' status, reject the operation with a conflict error.
- If the refund request does not exist, reject with a not-found error.
- If the authenticated seller does not own the refund request, reject with a forbidden error.

responseBody.description: The updated refund request reflecting the seller's decision. Includes the new status (approved or rejected), the response timestamp, and the customer's original reason.

parameters.name: refundRequestId

requestBody.description: Seller's decision on the refund request containing the new status value. Allowed values: "approved" to approve the refund (triggers stock restoration and status change), or "rejected" to deny the refund.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of refund request snapshots for a specific refund request.

Snapshots are immutable audit records automatically created whenever a seller responds to a refund request — either approving or rejecting it. Each snapshot preserves the customer's stated reason, the seller's decision (approved or rejected), and the exact timestamp when the seller responded, providing an unalterable audit trail for dispute resolution.

Results are sorted by creation date (newest first) and paginated for efficient browsing. Filtering is supported by snapshot status (approved or rejected) and date range on the response timestamp. Access is limited to the customer who submitted the original refund request, the seller who owns the product variant, and administrators with oversight permissions, as defined by the snapshot audit trail policy.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query e_commerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots table filtered by e_commerce_mall_refund_request_id matching the path parameter refundRequestId (UUID). Support pagination with page index and limit from the request body. Default sort order is created_at descending (newest first). Support optional filtering criteria: status (exact match for 'approved' or 'rejected'), response_timestamp range (from/to), and created_at range (from/to). Return IPageIECommerceMallRefundRequestSnapshot.ISummary with fields: id, reason, status, response_timestamp, created_at. Implement authorization: only the customer who created the parent refund request, the seller assigned to it, or administrators/superAdministrators may access. Since snapshots are immutable append-only records, ensure no update or delete operations are exposed. Ensure soft-deleted refund requests are excluded or handled per soft-delete policy (filter where parent refund_request.deleted_at IS NULL unless administrator override applies).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of refund request snapshot summary records. Each record contains the snapshot ID, the customer's stated reason for the refund, the seller's decision (approved or rejected), the timestamp when the seller responded, and the snapshot creation timestamp. Optimized for audit trail browsing and dispute resolution workflows.
