customer.description:
The customer who placed this order.

Each order belongs to exactly one customer. This association is preserved even after the customer deletes their account, ensuring order history remains intact for seller record-keeping and legal purposes. Includes the customer's email, profile information (display name, phone number), account creation date, and current status indicators (ban and soft-deletion status).
customer.x-autobe-specification: JOIN from e_commerce_mall_orders.e_commerce_mall_customer_id to e_commerce_mall_customers.id. Rendered as IECommerceMallCustomer.ISummary (id, email, profile, timestamps, ban and deletion status). Preserved even after customer account deletion for historical order integrity.

orderItems.description:
The purchased items in this order.

Each order item represents a specific product variant purchased with a given quantity. Items are tracked with independent fulfillment statuses (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded) because items from different sellers within the same order may be fulfilled separately. Each item includes historical snapshots preserving the product, variant, and seller profile state as they existed at the moment of purchase, ensuring a permanent audit trail for order histories and dispute resolution.
orderItems.x-autobe-specification: Composition JOIN from e_commerce_mall_order_items where e_commerce_mall_order_id = e_commerce_mall_orders.id. Rendered as IECommerceMallOrderItem[] (full detail with quantity, unit_price, status, timestamps, product-variant snapshot, seller snapshot, status logs, optional shipment, and optional cancellation/refund/review references).

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the order was created upon successful payment completion.

Used for chronological sorting of order history with newest-first ordering.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.created_at (Timestamptz). Set at order creation upon successful payment.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when the order was last updated.

Updated whenever any constituent order item transitions status (e.g., when items are shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded), which may change the derived overall order status.
updatedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.updated_at (Timestamptz). Updated when any constituent order item transitions status (e.g., shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded).

IECommerceMallOrder.description:
Complete order record containing purchased items, shipping address snapshot, customer information, and per-item fulfillment tracking.

Each order belongs to a single customer and contains one or more order items representing purchased product variants. The total price is calculated at order creation from the sum of all item subtotals and is immutable. The shipping address fields are snapshots captured at checkout — they are independent of the customer's current address records and do not change if the customer later edits their addresses.

The orderItems array provides the full details of each purchased item, including quantity, unit price at the time of purchase, independent fulfillment status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded), product-variant snapshots, seller profile snapshots captured at purchase time, and shipment tracking information.

The overall order status is not stored directly but is derived from the individual order item statuses at query time.
IECommerceMallOrder.x-autobe-specification: Direct column mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders for all scalar fields (id, code, total_price, shipping_* fields, created_at, updated_at). JOIN e_commerce_mall_customers via e_commerce_mall_customer_id for the customer relation (IECommerceMallCustomer.ISummary). Composition JOIN e_commerce_mall_order_items via e_commerce_mall_order_id for orderItems (IECommerceMallOrderItem[]). Orders are permanently preserved — no soft-delete filtering. No stored overall_order_status — derived at query time from constituent order item statuses.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the cart item.

This ID is used to reference the cart item when updating its quantity or removing it from the cart via the dedicated cart item endpoints.
id.x-autobe-specification: Maps from e_commerce_mall_cart_items.id. Primary key from the cart items table, included in this computed join result.

product.description:
Summary of the product this cart item belongs to.

Includes the product's name, base price, thumbnail image, seller shop name, category, average rating, and review count. The product name is displayed as the item's title in the cart view.
product.x-autobe-specification: Traverse from cart_item.productVariant → variant.product to retrieve IECommerceMallProduct.ISummary. Joins e_commerce_mall_products via e_commerce_mall_product_variants.e_commerce_mall_product_id.

variant.description:
Summary of the selected product variant (SKU) for this cart item.

Each cart item targets a specific variant configuration (e.g., color: Red, size: Large). The variant's effective price is used for the unit price calculation. If the variant has been deleted or is out of stock, the cart item is marked as unavailable for checkout.
variant.x-autobe-specification: Maps from e_commerce_mall_cart_items.productVariant relation. Returns IECommerceMallProductVariant.ISummary containing SKU code, options as key-value pairs, current stock quantity (SUM of inventory_records.quantity_change), and effective price (COALESCE variant.price, product.base_price).

options.description:
Key-value pairs describing the variant's configuration options (e.g., color='Red', size='Large').

Each option represents a single attribute dimension of the selected variant. The available option keys depend on how the seller configured the product's variants during setup.
options.x-autobe-specification: Traverse from cart_item.productVariant → variant.options. Collect rows from e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options where deleted_at IS NULL, grouped by variant_id, transformed into a key-value dictionary mapping option key to option value.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the product variant the customer intends to purchase.

Must be a positive integer. When the same variant is added to the cart again, quantities are combined into this single cart item rather than creating a duplicate entry.
quantity.x-autobe-specification: Maps from e_commerce_mall_cart_items.quantity. Must be a positive integer. Part of this computed join result.

unit_price.description:
Effective unit price for this cart item.

If the selected variant has a price override, that price is used. Otherwise, the product's base price is applied. This value is multiplied by the quantity to calculate the line subtotal.
unit_price.x-autobe-specification: Calculated as COALESCE(e_commerce_mall_product_variants.price, e_commerce_mall_products.base_price). Variant price override takes precedence; if null, the product's base price is used.

subtotal.description:
Line subtotal for this cart item.

Computed as the effective unit price multiplied by the quantity. Unavailable items are excluded from the overall cart total price calculation.
subtotal.x-autobe-specification: Calculated as unit_price × e_commerce_mall_cart_items.quantity. Line-level total for this cart item.

available.description:
Whether this cart item is available for checkout.

An item is marked as unavailable if the product variant has been deleted by the seller or if the current stock quantity is zero or less. Unavailable items remain visible in the cart for the customer to review but are excluded from checkout and the total price calculation.
available.x-autobe-specification: Computed as: variant.deleted_at IS NULL AND current_stock > 0. current_stock = SUM(e_commerce_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change) for that variant. An item is unavailable if the variant has been deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) or the sum of inventory changes is 0 or less.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this cart item was first added to the cart.

Cart items are displayed in the order they were added, with the earliest-added item appearing first and the most recently added item appearing last.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Maps from e_commerce_mall_cart_items.created_at. Items sorted by this field in ascending order (oldest first, most recent last). Part of this computed join result.

IECommerceMallCartOverview.description:
Cart overview response containing the list of cart items with full product and variant details.

Each cart item displays the product name, selected variant options (e.g., color, size), effective unit price, quantity, line subtotal, and availability status. The total price of all available items is computed and returned. Unavailable items — where the product variant has been deleted or is out of stock — are clearly marked and excluded from the total price calculation. Cart items are sorted by the order they were added, oldest first.
IECommerceMallCartOverview.x-autobe-specification: Computed response type for customer cart overview endpoint. Joins e_commerce_mall_cart_items (filtered by customer_id from JWT, deleted_at IS NULL) with e_commerce_mall_product_variants and e_commerce_mall_products. Options grouped from e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options key-value pairs. Stock derived from SUM(e_commerce_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change). unit_price = COALESCE(variant.price, product.base_price). subtotal = unit_price × quantity. available = variant.deleted_at IS NULL AND stock > 0. Sorted by cart_items.created_at ASC.

topLevelCategories.description:
An array of top-level categories representing the root nodes of the two-level category hierarchy.

Each top-level category is a broad grouping (e.g., "Electronics") that contains its own nested subcategories in a subcategories array. Top-level categories are those with no parent category (parent_id is null), ordered by creation date ascending. Subcategories within each parent are also ordered by creation date ascending.

When a name-based search filter is applied, this array includes only those top-level categories that either match the filter directly or have subcategories that match — ensuring customers can navigate to matching subcategories with their full hierarchy context preserved.
topLevelCategories.x-autobe-specification: Computed array: query e_commerce_mall_categories WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND parent_id IS NULL, ordered by created_at ASC. For each top-level category, query subcategories WHERE parent_id = this.id AND deleted_at IS NULL, ordered by created_at ASC. Each resulting IHierarchyNode contains direct category fields plus nested subcategories array. If a name search filter is provided, filter all categories by case-insensitive partial name match FIRST, then for any matching subcategory, include its parent in the top-level result set regardless of whether the parent itself matches the filter.

IECommerceMallCategory.IHierarchy.description:
The complete category hierarchy tree containing all non-deleted categories organized in a two-level parent-child structure.

Top-level categories represent broad groupings (e.g., "Electronics") and each contains an array of subcategories representing more specific classifications (e.g., "Smartphones", "Laptops"). Only two levels of nesting are supported — subcategories cannot contain further subcategories, enforcing the two-level depth constraint.

Soft-deleted categories (those with a deleted_at timestamp) are excluded from the result, ensuring that only active categories appear in browseable listings. When a name-based search filter is provided, matching subcategories cause their parent top-level category to be included in the result, preserving the hierarchy context for filtered views.
IECommerceMallCategory.IHierarchy.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: query e_commerce_mall_categories WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Segregate rows into top-level (parent_id IS NULL) and subcategories (parent_id IS NOT NULL). If name search filter is provided, apply case-insensitive partial matching on the name column. When a subcategory matches, include its parent top-level category. Build response by nesting subcategories under their parent via parent_id matching. Order top-level by created_at ASC, subcategories under each parent by created_at ASC. Edge cases: empty result returns empty topLevelCategories array; all categories soft-deleted returns empty structure; top-level with no subcategories returns empty subcategories array within its node.

refundedItems.description:
Array of order items that were successfully refunded.

Each item represents an order item whose status was changed to `refunded` during this force-refund operation. A status log entry recording the transition and a positive inventory record restoring stock quantity are created for each refunded item.

Empty array when no eligible items were found to refund.
refundedItems.x-autobe-specification: Order items whose status was successfully changed to 'refunded' during the force-refund operation. Collected by iterating over the target order items, changing status to 'refunded', and appending to this array. Each item is rendered as IECommerceMallOrderItem.ISummary via re-query from e_commerce_mall_order_items after the transaction completes. Never null — empty array when no items were refunded.

skippedItems.description:
Array of order items that were skipped during the force-refund operation, with reasons explaining why each could not be refunded.

Items are skipped when they are already in a terminal state (`cancelled` or `refunded`), or when the requested item ID does not belong to the specified order.

Empty array when no items were skipped.
skippedItems.x-autobe-specification: Order items that were skipped during the force-refund operation and the reasons they could not be refunded. Collected by iterating over target order items and appending items that are already in 'cancelled' or 'refunded' terminal state (skip reason: 'already in terminal state'), or items from the request's orderItemIds that don't belong to the specified order (skip reason: 'item does not belong to this order'). Each entry includes the IECommerceMallOrderItem.ISummary and a reason string. Never null — empty array when no items were skipped.

IECommerceMallOrder.IForceRefundResponse.description:
Summary of the force-refund operation results.

Contains two lists: the order items that were successfully refunded (status changed to 'refunded'), and the order items that were skipped during the operation along with the reasons they could not be refunded (e.g., already in cancelled or refunded terminal state).

When no orderItemIds are specified in the request body, all eligible items in the order are included in the refunded list, and already-terminal items are in the skipped list.
IECommerceMallOrder.IForceRefundResponse.x-autobe-specification:
Computed response assembled after executing a force-refund operation within a database transaction.

refundedItems: Order items whose status was successfully changed to 'refunded'. For each such item, an e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs entry is created (from_status = current status, to_status = 'refunded', reason = 'administrator_force_refund'), and a positive e_commerce_mall_inventory_records entry is created (quantity_change = item.quantity, reason = 'force-refunded') for the associated product variant.

skippedItems: Order items that could not be refunded because they were already in a terminal state ('cancelled' or 'refunded'), or items from the request's orderItemIds that do not belong to the specified order. Each entry includes the order item summary and the reason for skipping.

If request body orderItemIds is omitted or empty, ALL eligible order items in the order are processed. If provided, only those specific order items are targeted (with validation that they belong to the specified order).

item.description:
The order item that was skipped during the force-refund operation.

Provides the full order item summary including the product name and variant options as they existed at the time of purchase (from product-variant snapshots), the seller's shop name at the time of purchase (from seller snapshot), the quantity purchased, unit price, calculated subtotal, current fulfillment status, and references to the parent order and product variant.

When the order item with the specified ID does not belong to the target order, the skip reason takes precedence and the item summary is not populated.
item.x-autobe-specification: Fetched from e_commerce_mall_order_items via the orderItemId provided in the force-refund request body. Rendered as IECommerceMallOrderItem.ISummary which includes: flattened snapshot data (product_name, variant_sku, variant_options via 1:1 JOIN on order_item_snapshots table; shop_name via 1:1 JOIN on order_item_seller_snapshots table), direct columns (id, quantity, unit_price, status, created_at), computed subtotal (quantity * unit_price at application layer), and BELONGS-TO relations (order via e_commerce_mall_order_id as IECommerceMallOrder.ISummary, productVariant via e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id as IECommerceMallProductVariant.ISummary). If the orderItemId from the request body does not correspond to any order item belonging to the target order (identified by the orderCode path parameter), the skip reason takes precedence and the item summary is not computed.

reason.description:
The reason why this order item could not be refunded.

Possible values:
- `already in terminal state`: The item's status is `cancelled` or `refunded`, which are terminal states that cannot be further transitioned.
- `item does not belong to this order`: The item ID was provided in the `orderItemIds` request array but does not belong to the order identified by the `orderCode` path parameter.

Only items that could not be refunded appear in this skipped items list — items that were successfully force-refunded are not included here.
reason.x-autobe-specification:
Determined by the force-refund operation logic at runtime. Evaluated in priority order:
1. First, check if the requested orderItemId (from the force-refund request body's `orderItemIds` array) belongs to the target order (identified by orderCode path parameter). If not, reason = 'item does not belong to this order'.
2. If it does belong to the order, check if e_commerce_mall_order_items.status is 'cancelled' or 'refunded' (terminal states that cannot be further transitioned). If yes, reason = 'already in terminal state'.
Only items that could not be refunded appear in this skipped items list — items that were successfully force-refunded are not included here.

IECommerceMallOrder.IForceRefundSkippedI.description:
An order item that was skipped during a force-refund operation, with an explanation of why it could not be refunded.

Items are skipped when they are already in a terminal state (`cancelled` or `refunded`), or when the requested item ID from the `orderItemIds` list does not belong to the specified order.

The {@link item} field provides the order item summary for identification and the {@link reason} field explains why the item was excluded from the force-refund operation.

This object is returned as part of the {@link IECommerceMallOrder.IForceRefundResponse.skippedItems} array when the force-refund operation encounters items that cannot be processed.
IECommerceMallOrder.IForceRefundSkippedI.x-autobe-specification: Computed response object assembled during the force-refund operation. The `item` field is fetched from e_commerce_mall_order_items using the orderItemId from the request body and rendered as IECommerceMallOrderItem.ISummary (which internally flattens snapshot data from order_item_snapshots and order_item_seller_snapshots via 1:1 JOINs, plus BELONGS-TO relations to order and productVariant). The `reason` field is determined by the operation logic: 'already in terminal state' when the order item's status is 'cancelled' or 'refunded', or 'item does not belong to this order' when a requested orderItemId from the request body does not match any order item belonging to the target order (identified by the orderCode path parameter).

id.description:
Unique identifier for this product snapshot image record.

This is the primary key of the preserved image entry within the parent product snapshot, used for referencing individual snapshot images in API responses.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_images.id. UUID primary key, immutable.

url.description:
The historical image URL preserved at the time of the product snapshot.

Contains the exact URL (typically a file storage reference) of the product image as it existed when the parent product snapshot was created. This URL is an immutable record — it will never change and points to the version of the image archived at snapshot time for historical accuracy.
url.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_images.url. Stored as VarChar(80000) in the database — represents a file storage URL reference.

sort_order.description:
Display order of this image within the snapshot's image collection.

Lower values indicate higher priority. The first image (sort_order = 0) serves as the thumbnail representation of the product at the time the snapshot was taken. Images are returned in ascending order by sort_order in array responses, reflecting their arrangement at the moment of capture.
sort_order.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_images.sort_order. Integer starting at 0, ascending order. Indexed together with parent snapshot ID for ordered retrieval.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this snapshot image record was created.

Since snapshot records are immutable, this field indicates the exact moment the image state was captured as part of the parent product snapshot creation. Serves as the chronological reference point for when this particular image arrangement was archived.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_images.created_at. Timestamptz format. Immutable — this is the timestamp of when the image state was captured as part of the parent snapshot creation.

IECommerceMallProductSnapshot.IImage.description:
A preserved product image within a product snapshot, capturing the image URL and display order as they existed at the moment the snapshot was created.

Product snapshot images are immutable records created atomically as part of the parent {@link IECommerceMallProductSnapshot}. They preserve how a product's visual representation appeared at a specific point in time for dispute resolution and audit purposes.

{@link url} contains the exact image URL (typically a file storage reference) as archived at snapshot time.
{@link sort_order} determines the display sequence — lower values indicate higher priority, where the first image (sort_order = 0) serves as the thumbnail. Images are ordered ascending by sort_order in array responses.
IECommerceMallProductSnapshot.IImage.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_images: id, url, sort_order, created_at. Sort_order is ascending (lower = higher priority). Immutable record — updated_at always equals created_at (omitted from DTO), deleted_at is always null (omitted). Created atomically as part of parent product snapshot creation. This is a read-only DTO embedded within IECommerceMallProductSnapshot.snapshotImages array; no create/update/delete operations target this schema directly.

key.description:
The option name identifying this attribute dimension (e.g., 'color', 'size', 'material').

This key defines which attribute dimension of the variant is being described. Combined with the parent variant's ID, each key must be unique within that variant, ensuring no duplicate option types exist. For example, a variant cannot have two options both with key 'color'.

value.description:
The option value describing this dimension for the variant (e.g., 'Red', 'Large', 'Cotton').

This value represents the actual selection for the option key within this specific variant's configuration. For example, a variant with key 'color' might have the value 'Red', and a variant with key 'size' might have the value 'Large'.

IECommerceMallProductVariant.IOption.description:
A single option key-value pair defining a distinguishing attribute of a product variant.

Each option represents one configuration dimension such as color, size, or material. Together, the set of options uniquely identifies this variant among all variants of the same product. For example, a variant might have options [{ key: 'color', value: 'Red' }, { key: 'size', value: 'Large' }].
IECommerceMallProductVariant.IOption.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options. key maps to key (String), value maps to value (String). Both are required. The e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id FK is set automatically when the parent variant record is created. id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at are auto-generated/system-managed fields not exposed in this DTO.

id.description:
The unique identifier of the seller's shop profile.

This UUID is the primary key of the seller profile record and serves as the stable reference for linking to seller details across the platform.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_seller_profiles.id. UUID primary key.

id.description:

Assigned automatically when the parent product snapshot is created during a product edit. Used as the primary key for identifying specific variant snapshots within the product snapshot's variant collection.

sku.description:

name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_variants.name. Stores the formatted display name combining variant option values (e.g., 'Red / Large').

price.description:
The variant's own price at the time of snapshot creation, if it had one.

A variant can optionally override the product's base price with its own price. This field captures that override value. When null, the variant did not have its own price and the product's base price (preserved in the parent snapshot) applied to this variant at that time.
price.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_variants.price. Nullable Double (Float?) — when null, it means the variant did not have its own price override and the product's base price (preserved in the parent IECommerceMallProductSnapshot) applied to this variant at that time.

created_at.description:
The timestamp when this variant snapshot was created.

Corresponds to the moment the parent product snapshot was generated upon a product edit. Establishes the historical context of when the variant's state was captured. Matches the parent product snapshot's creation timestamp.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_variants.created_at. Timestamptz, matches the parent snapshot's creation timestamp.

IECommerceMallProductSnapshot.IVariant.description:
A preserved variant configuration within a product snapshot.

Represents the complete state of a single product variant (stock-keeping unit) as it existed at the moment the parent product snapshot was created. Each record captures the variant's unique SKU code, a human-readable display name combining option values (e.g., 'Red / Large'), an optional price override, and the creation timestamp.

Variant snapshots are immutable — they are created atomically alongside the parent product snapshot whenever a seller edits their product and are never modified or deleted thereafter. They survive deletion of the original variant or product, ensuring a complete audit trail for dispute resolution, policy enforcement, and historical reference. This type is used when viewing a product snapshot's variant collection via the snapshot detail endpoint.
IECommerceMallProductSnapshot.IVariant.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_variants table. All fields are immutable snapshot records — no JOINs or transformations needed. id → UUID primary key, sku → unique SKU identifier, name → display name combining variant option values, price → nullable Double (null when variant used product's base price), created_at → snapshot creation timestamp. The parent FK (e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_id) and the belongs-to snapshot relation are omitted as this type is a nested sub-schema accessed within the parent snapshot context.

name.description:
The display name of the category.

A short descriptive label such as 'Electronics' or 'Clothing' that identifies the category for customers browsing the product catalog. Must clearly convey what types of products belong here.

description.description:
A textual explanation of the category's scope.

Helps customers understand what types of products belong in this category when navigating the catalog hierarchy.

parent.description:
The parent category in the two-level hierarchy.

When non-null, this category is a subcategory belonging to the referenced parent (e.g., 'Smartphones' under 'Electronics'). When null, this category is a top-level category. Only one level of nesting is supported — subcategories cannot have further subcategories.

Only one level of nesting is supported — a subcategory cannot itself be a parent to further subcategories. Resolved as IECommerceMallCategory.ISummary.

subcategories.description:
Child categories belonging to this top-level parent.

Contains the direct subcategories organized under this parent, each represented as a full IHierarchyNode to support recursive tree rendering. Empty array for leaf subcategories and for top-level categories that have no children assigned.

Provides quick context on the quantity of products available within this category for browsing. Computed dynamically rather than stored.

created_at.description: The timestamp when the category was first created by an administrator.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_categories.created_at.

updated_at.description:
The timestamp when the category was last modified.

Updated whenever name, description, or parent relationship is changed by an administrator.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_categories.updated_at.

deleted_at.description:
The timestamp when the category was soft-deleted.

When present, the category has been deleted by an administrator. Soft deletion preserves referential integrity with existing product references and snapshot records. Products assigned to a deleted category become uncategorized.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_categories.deleted_at. Null when the category is active. Non-null indicates soft-deletion by an administrator.

IECommerceMallCategory.IHierarchyNode.description:
A single node in the product category hierarchy tree, representing a category with its position in the two-level parent-child structure and contextual metadata.

Each node corresponds to a non-deleted category and contains its identifying information (id, name, description), hierarchy navigation fields (parent for subcategories, subcategories array for top-level categories), and contextual data (products_count for the number of active products assigned).

The subcategories array contains nested IHierarchyNode objects for the children of top-level categories, or is empty for leaf subcategories. The parent field references the parent category's summary when this node is a subcategory, or is null for top-level categories. Only two levels of nesting are supported — subcategories cannot have further subcategories, so nested nodes always have an empty subcategories array.
IECommerceMallCategory.IHierarchyNode.x-autobe-specification: Direct columns (id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) mapped from e_commerce_mall_categories. parent: self-join via parent_id FK to same table, resolved as IECommerceMallCategory.ISummary (null when parent_id IS NULL). subcategories: self-join where parent_id = this.id AND deleted_at IS NULL, each child mapped recursively as IHierarchyNode (empty array for leaf subcategories). products_count: COUNT on e_commerce_mall_products WHERE category_id = this.id AND deleted_at IS NULL. All queries filtered WHERE deleted_at IS NULL to exclude soft-deleted categories.

IECommerceMallProductVariantOption.description:
A single key-value pair option that defines one dimension of a product variant's distinguishing configuration.

Each option represents an attribute such as color, size, or material. Together, the set of options uniquely identifies a variant among all variants of the same product. For example, a variant with key 'color' and value 'Red' indicates the variant is the red configuration of the product.

Each variant has at most one value per option key, enforced by a unique constraint on the combination of variant and key. Only active (non-deleted) options are returned in responses.

Only active options (deleted_at IS NULL) are returned. The parent variant context is established by the owning variant's options array, so e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id (FK) and the variant relation are not exposed in this DTO. System timestamps (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are excluded as they are managed by the database layer.

action.description:
Comma-separated list of action types to filter audit log entries by.

Filters the unified audit log to only include entries whose action type matches one of the specified values. Action types include force_cancel_order_item, force_refund_order_item, ban_customer, unban_customer, suspend_seller, unsuspend_seller, approve_seller, reject_seller, delete_product, create_category, edit_category, delete_category, admin_promotion, admin_demotion, admin_request_approval, and admin_request_rejection. When omitted, entries of all action types are returned.

When specified, filter UNION results to only include entries whose action matches one of the listed values.

targetType.description:
Entity type to filter audit log entries by.

Restricts the results to only include entries where the target entity type matches the specified value. Supported target types include order_item, customer, seller, product, category, seller_approval_request, administrator, and admin_registration_request. When omitted, entries targeting any entity type are returned.
targetType.x-autobe-specification: Entity type filter. Maps to target_type in both audit log tables. When specified, filter UNION results to only include entries where target_type matches the given value.

actorType.description:
Actor type to restrict the audit log results to.

Use 'administrator' to return only actions performed by regular administrators, 'superAdministrator' for only super administrator actions, or 'both' (default when omitted) to include entries from both actor types. This filter determines which underlying audit log tables are queried — the regular administrator audit log table, the super administrator audit log table, or both combined.
actorType.x-autobe-specification: Actor type discriminator. 'administrator' queries only e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs, 'superAdministrator' queries only e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs, 'both' (default when omitted) UNIONs both tables.

from.description:
Start of the date range filter for audit log entries.

Only entries with a created_at timestamp greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 datetime value are returned. Use this together with the 'to' parameter to define a time-bounded search window. When omitted, no lower bound is applied.
from.x-autobe-specification: ISO 8601 datetime. Apply filter: created_at >= from in both audit log tables. When omitted, no lower bound is applied.

to.description:
End of the date range filter for audit log entries.

Only entries with a created_at timestamp less than or equal to this ISO 8601 datetime value are returned. Use this together with the 'from' parameter to define a time-bounded search window. When omitted, no upper bound is applied.
to.x-autobe-specification: ISO 8601 datetime. Apply filter: created_at <= to in both audit log tables. When omitted, no upper bound is applied.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results.

Indicates which page of results to return. Page numbering starts at 1. The total number of pages available is returned in the pagination metadata of the response. Defaults to 1 when omitted.
page.x-autobe-specification: Page number for pagination. Defaults to 1. Used to calculate offset: (page - 1) * limit. Minimum value is 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many audit log entries are returned in a single page. The actual number of records may be less than this value on the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit. Defaults to 20 when omitted. Maximum allowed value is 100.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Defaults to 20. Maximum allowed is 100. Used as the LIMIT clause in queries.

sort.description:
Sort order for results by creation timestamp.

'desc' (default) returns the newest entries first, listing the most recent administrative actions at the top. 'asc' returns the oldest entries first for chronological review of the audit trail.
sort.x-autobe-specification: Sort order on created_at. 'desc' (default) sorts newest first (ORDER BY created_at DESC), 'asc' sorts oldest first (ORDER BY created_at ASC).

IECommerceMallSuperAdministratorAuditLog.description:
Search and filter criteria for retrieving platform audit logs.

Provides filtering parameters to narrow down audit log entries by action type, target entity type, actor type (regular administrator or super administrator), and a date range defined by from/to timestamps. Supports pagination via page and limit parameters, and sort ordering by creation timestamp. All filter parameters are optional — omitting all filters returns the complete audit log sorted by newest entries first.
IECommerceMallSuperAdministratorAuditLog.x-autobe-specification: Source: UNION of e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs and e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs. Filters: action (comma-separated list, mapped to action_type in admin logs and action in super-admin logs), targetType (maps to target_type in both tables), actorType ('administrator'/'superAdministrator'/'both', determines which table(s) to query), from (ISO datetime, filter created_at >= from in both tables), to (ISO datetime, filter created_at <= to in both tables). Pagination: page (default 1), limit (default 20, max 100). Sort: 'desc' (default) or 'asc' on created_at.

id.description:
The unique identifier for this audit log entry.

This UUID primary key uniquely identifies a single administrative action recorded in the platform's immutable audit trail, enabling precise cross-referencing and retrieval of individual audit records. It originates from the source audit log table (either regular administrator or super administrator) where the action was originally recorded.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the `id` column of either e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs or e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs, depending on the source table of each record. UUID primary key from the originating audit log table.

action.description:
The type of administrative action that was performed.

This field contains the normalized action type identifying what specific administrative operation was executed. Examples include: seller_suspension, seller_unsuspension, approve_seller, reject_seller, customer_ban, customer_unban, seller_ban, force_cancel_order_item, force_refund_order_item, delete_product, create_category, edit_category, delete_category, admin_promotion, admin_demotion, admin_request_approval, and admin_request_rejection.
action.x-autobe-specification: Normalized from e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs.action_type (snake_case, e.g., force_cancel_order_item) or e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs.action (snake_case). Map both source columns to the same normalized 'action' field. Keep the same snake_case value used in both source tables.

actor_type.description:
The type of administrator who performed this action.

This discriminator field indicates whether the action was performed by a regular administrator ('administrator') or a super administrator ('superAdministrator'), enabling unified querying across both regular and super administrator audit log tables. When the value is 'administrator', the actor_id references e_commerce_mall_administrators; when 'superAdministrator', it references e_commerce_mall_super_administrators.
actor_type.x-autobe-specification: Computed constant value: set to 'administrator' when the record originates from e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs, and 'superAdministrator' when the record originates from e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs. This discriminator enables downstream consumers to know which audit table the record came from and which actor_id resolution to use.

actor_id.description:
The unique identifier of the administrator who performed this action.

References the administrator or super administrator account that executed the action. For regular administrator actions (actor_type: 'administrator'), this is the UUID from the administrators table. For super administrator actions (actor_type: 'superAdministrator'), this is the UUID from the super administrators table.
actor_id.x-autobe-specification: Maps to e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs.e_commerce_mall_administrator_id for regular administrator records, or e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs.e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_id for super administrator records. The actor_type field determines which FK column to use.

actor_email.description:
The email address of the administrator who performed this action.

Provides a human-readable identifier for the acting administrator, sourced from the corresponding administrator account record via a join on the actor's foreign key. This enables quick identification of who performed the action without requiring a separate lookup.
actor_email.x-autobe-specification: Computed via LEFT JOIN: for regular administrator records, join e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs.e_commerce_mall_administrator_id to e_commerce_mall_administrators.id and extract email. For super administrator records, join e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs.e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_id to e_commerce_mall_super_administrators.id and extract email.

target_type.description:
The type of entity that was the target of this administrative action.

This polymorphic discriminator identifies the kind of entity that was affected. Examples include: order_item, customer, seller, product, category, seller_approval_request, admin_registration_request, and administrator. This field enables entity-scoped queries of the audit trail, such as retrieving all actions performed on a particular entity type.
target_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the `target_type` column of either source table (e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs or e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs). Both tables use the same polymorphic target_type column with the same naming convention.

target_id.description:
The unique identifier of the specific entity that this action was performed on.

Stores the UUID of the affected entity (e.g., the customer_id for a ban action, the order_item_id for a force-cancel action, the seller_id for a suspension action). Used together with target_type to polymorphically reference any platform entity, enabling complete cross-referencing with the affected record for audit trail traceability.
target_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the `target_id` column of either source table (e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs or e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs). Both tables use the same polymorphic target_id column with UUID format.

reason.description:
An optional textual explanation for why this action was taken.

Required for certain actions such as seller registration rejections, customer bans, product deletions, and admin request rejections to provide transparency and justification for the administrative decision. May be null for self-explanatory actions where the action type alone provides sufficient context.
reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the `reason` column of either source table. Both tables have an optional nullable reason field. Pass through as-is, preserving null for actions where no reason was provided.

created_at.description:
The timestamp when this audit log entry was created.

Represents the exact moment the administrative action was performed and recorded in the audit trail. This timestamp enables chronological ordering of audit events, time-based filtering, and historical analysis of administrative activity on the platform.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the `created_at` column of either source table (e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs or e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs). Both tables use timestamptz for this field.

IECommerceMallSuperAdministratorAuditLog.description:
Summary representation of a platform audit log entry, combining actions from both regular administrators and super administrators into a unified view.

Each entry captures a single administrative action recorded in the platform's immutable audit trail. The actor_type field discriminates whether the action was performed by a regular administrator or a super administrator, with the actor's email provided for identification. The action field contains the normalized action type (e.g., seller_suspension, admin_promotion, force_cancel_order_item). The polymorphic target_type and target_id fields reference the affected entity (customer, seller, product, order item, category, administrator, etc.), enabling cross-referencing with the target record.
IECommerceMallSuperAdministratorAuditLog.x-autobe-specification: UNION of e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs and e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs. Normalize action: map administrator_audit_logs.action_type and super_administrator_audit_logs.action to a common 'action' field. Set actor_type: 'administrator' for records from administrator_audit_logs, 'superAdministrator' for records from super_administrator_audit_logs. Set actor_id: e_commerce_mall_administrator_id for regular logs, e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_id for super admin logs. Join e_commerce_mall_administrators and e_commerce_mall_super_administrators on their respective FK columns to include actor_email. Keep the polymorphic target_type+target_id pattern unchanged.
